def factor_volatility_spread_reversal(df):
    """Capture reversal tendency under high volatility regime spread.
    Uses ratio of short-term to long-term historical volatility to scale
    recent return reversal."""
    df_copy = df.copy()
    # Compute daily returns
    ret = df_copy["close"].pct_change()
    # Short-term and long-term realized volatility
    short_vol = ret.rolling(5, min_periods=5).std()
    long_vol = ret.rolling(20, min_periods=20).std()
    # Volatility regime indicator: ratio of short to long vol
    vol_ratio = short_vol / long_vol.replace(0, np.nan)
    # Reversal signal: negative of recent 5-day return
    recent_ret = df_copy["close"] / df_copy["close"].shift(5) - 1
    reversal = -recent_ret
    # Scale reversal by volatility ratio to amplify in high vol regimes
    factor = reversal * vol_ratio
    # Pasteurize: replace inf and fillna
    factor = factor.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).fillna(0)
    df_copy["factor_volatility_spread_reversal"] = factor
    return df_copy["factor_volatility_spread_reversal"]
description: During high volatility regimes, when short-term volatility exceeds long-term volatility, recent price movements are more likely to reverse. This factor combines a short-term reversal signal scaled by the ratio of short-term to long-term realized volatility, emphasizing mean-reversion signals in elevated volatility states.
